projects.title: FreelancersDesk
projects.subtitle: n8n Workflow Automation Suite
projects.role: Solo Builder for architecture, workflow design, and integrations
projects.tagline: I built an end-to-end operations assistant for freelancers to automate job discovery, proposal drafting, payment tracking, and personal branding, all running on autopilot.
projects.description: I built a connected suite of n8n workflows to run the operational side of freelancing. It finds remote jobs, drafts proposals, tracks applications in Google Sheets, monitors payments, sends invoice reminders, and posts updates to LinkedIn.
projects.problem: Freelancers lose hours every week to work that isn't billable: scanning job boards, writing near-identical proposals, remembering which client still owes money, and keeping a professional presence alive online. None of it is hard — it's just constant.
projects.solution: I built a chain of n8n workflows that treats the whole freelance pipeline as one system. Jobs are fetched and scored automatically and pushed to Telegram with a ready proposal attached. A single tap logs the application to Google Sheets, which then becomes the source of truth for payment tracking and reminder emails. A separate workflow reads project progress and turns it into a weekly LinkedIn post.
features: Fetches remote job listings and pushes them straight to Telegram as direct notifications
Each notification bundles a job link, a match score, and a pre-drafted proposal
One-tap 'Applied' action writes the job details into Google Sheets
Tracks paid vs. unpaid clients across the full project ledger
Sends polite, automated follow-up emails for outstanding invoices
Monitors project progress and generates weekly LinkedIn career posts
outcomes: Removed manual job-board scanning from the daily routine
Made invoice follow-up consistent instead of dependent on memory
Kept a weekly publishing cadence with no manual writing

projects.title: AI CV Screening & JD Matching
projects.subtitle: NLP Document Intelligence
projects.role: AI/ML Engineer responsible for the parsing pipeline, matching logic, and scoring
projects.tagline: I built an NLP system that reads a stack of resumes and ranks candidates against the job description in seconds.
projects.description: I developed an NLP system that parses unstructured resumes, extracts skills, experience, and education into a structured profile, then scores each candidate against a target job description using semantic similarity rather than brittle keyword matching.
projects.problem: Manual CV screening is slow, inconsistent, and biased toward whoever happens to be at the top of the pile. Keyword filters fail the moment a candidate writes 'PyTorch' where the JD says 'deep learning frameworks'.
projects.solution: I designed a pipeline that extracts text from mixed-format CVs, normalizes it, and semantically compares candidate profiles to the job description so related terminology matches. The system provides a ranked score with matching details to give recruiters an instant shortlist.
features: Parses PDF and document-format CVs into structured candidate profiles
Extracts skills, work history, education, and contact details
Semantic matching against job descriptions — not literal keyword overlap
Ranked candidate scoring with match explanation
Bulk processing for high-volume roles
Exportable shortlists for handoff to hiring managers
outcomes: Cut first-pass screening from hours to minutes
Made ranking consistent across every candidate in a batch
Surfaced qualified candidates that keyword filters missed

projects.title: Customer Intent Detection
projects.subtitle: NLP Classification + Automated Support
projects.role: AI/ML Engineer responsible for the classifier, response routing, and API integration
projects.tagline: I developed an NLP classification model that identifies what a customer wants from their message to either answer it or route it to the right person.
projects.description: I built an intent-classification system that reads inbound customer messages, identifies the underlying request, and triggers the right automated response. Ambiguous or high-stakes messages are escalated to a human instead of being answered badly.
projects.problem: Support inboxes are dominated by a handful of repeated questions, but they arrive phrased a hundred different ways. Teams either answer them all manually or deploy a rigid bot that frustrates everyone.
projects.solution: I trained an intent classifier on labelled support conversations and wired it into an automated response layer. High-confidence intents get an instant, accurate answer; low-confidence or sensitive ones get flagged and handed to a human with the predicted intent attached as context.
features: Multi-class intent classification across common support categories
Confidence thresholding with automatic human escalation
Automated response generation for recognised intents
Handles varied phrasing, typos, and informal language
Deployable to WhatsApp, Telegram, and web chat
Logs predictions for ongoing model improvement
outcomes: Automated resolution of repetitive, high-volume queries
Reduced first-response time on common requests
Gave agents pre-classified context on escalated tickets

projects.title: Bank Fraud Detection
projects.subtitle: Imbalanced Classification
projects.role: ML Engineer responsible for feature engineering, modeling, and evaluation
projects.tagline: I built a model that catches the rare fraudulent transaction hiding inside millions of legitimate ones.
projects.description: I trained a supervised classification model that flags potentially fraudulent bank transactions in real time, built around the core difficulty of fraud detection: the positive class is vanishingly rare, and both false positives and false negatives are expensive in different ways.
projects.problem: Fraud makes up a tiny fraction of transactions, so a model that predicts 'legitimate' every time still scores high accuracy while being completely useless. Meanwhile, over-flagging blocks real customers and erodes trust.
projects.solution: I engineered transactional and behavioural features, applied class-imbalance handling, and evaluated on precision-recall rather than raw accuracy. The decision threshold is tunable, so the business can choose where it wants to sit on the trade-off between missed fraud and customer friction.
features: Feature engineering from transaction amount, timing, and behavioural patterns
Class-imbalance handling via resampling and class weighting
Model comparison across multiple classification algorithms
Precision-recall and ROC-AUC evaluation rather than accuracy alone
Tunable decision threshold for business risk appetite
Feature-importance analysis for explainability
outcomes: Reliable detection of the minority fraud class
Explainable flags rather than black-box rejections
Threshold controls that let risk teams set their own balance

projects.title: Facial Emotion Recognition
projects.subtitle: Computer Vision
projects.role: ML Engineer responsible for the data pipeline, model training, and evaluation
projects.tagline: I built a convolutional neural network to read emotional states from facial expressions.
projects.description: I developed a computer vision model that classifies facial expressions into emotion categories from image input, covering the full pipeline from face detection and preprocessing through CNN training and evaluation.
projects.problem: Emotion is signalled through subtle, overlapping facial cues, and image data varies wildly in lighting, angle, and resolution. Naive models collapse the moment conditions shift.
projects.solution: I built a preprocessing pipeline that detects and normalises faces before they reach the model, then trained a convolutional network with augmentation to survive real-world variation in lighting and pose.
features: Face detection and cropping preprocessing stage
Image normalisation and data augmentation
CNN architecture for multi-class emotion classification
Confusion-matrix analysis across emotion categories
Support for both static image and webcam frame input
outcomes: Robust classification across varied lighting and pose
Per-emotion performance breakdown for targeted improvement

projects.title: House Price Prediction
projects.subtitle: Regression Modelling
projects.role: ML Engineer responsible for exploratory data analysis, feature engineering, and model tuning
projects.tagline: I built regression models to predict property values from location, size, and condition, identifying which factors drive the price.
projects.description: I designed a regression model that estimates residential property prices from structural, locational, and condition-based features, with emphasis on interpretability so the prediction can be justified rather than just produced.
projects.problem: Property pricing depends on dozens of interacting factors, and raw housing data is messy — missing values, skewed distributions, and categorical variables everywhere.
projects.solution: I ran thorough exploratory data analysis, handled missing and skewed data, encoded categorical features, and compared several regression approaches with cross-validation before tuning the strongest performer.
features: Exploratory data analysis with correlation and distribution profiling
Missing-value imputation and outlier treatment
Categorical encoding and feature scaling
Model comparison: linear, tree-based, and ensemble regressors
Cross-validation and hyperparameter tuning
Feature-importance ranking for price drivers
outcomes: Accurate price estimates with quantified error margins
Clear ranking of which features most influence value

projects.title: Employee Salary Prediction
projects.subtitle: HR Analytics
projects.role: ML Engineer responsible for data preparation, modeling, and interpretation
projects.tagline: I built regression models to estimate fair compensation from experience, role, and education by leveraging my HR background.
projects.description: I developed a regression model predicting employee salary from role, experience, education, and workforce attributes, drawing directly on my domain expertise in HR.
projects.problem: Compensation decisions are often made on intuition and inconsistent benchmarks, which creates pay inequity and makes offers hard to defend.
projects.solution: I built a model that learns the relationship between employee attributes and compensation, giving HR teams a data-backed reference point and exposing which factors carry real weight in the existing pay structure.
features: Data cleaning and preparation of workforce attribute data
Encoding of role, department, and education categories
Regression modelling with performance evaluation
Feature-importance analysis on compensation drivers
Benchmark output usable for offer and review decisions
outcomes: Objective salary benchmarks to support HR decisions
Visibility into which attributes actually drive existing pay levels
